data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues the opposite side—that decentralized networks are more fragile to 'metabolic' correlated failures of shared infrastructure—but it never supplies the evidentiary discriminator the problem requires: how to tell genuinely independent failures from ones that only look uncorrelated until a shared cause is found. Its mechanism points to a low-level shared utility (regional power grid, primary internet exchange) as the hidden shared cause, yet it does not specify what evidence would reveal such clustering ex ante versus after the fact, nor how one would operationally distinguish the two regimes. The counterconditions (global distribution, large-service core-logic failure) identify cases where the fragility claim might not hold, but they are not framed as evidentiary tests of independence versus masked correlation.
